translations.t0039: Bernasconi routinely works on the scratch arrays and knows the infrastructure. The alley-door access was open (IV03-L37; she herself enquired about the door, HD-L130). No badge evidence, no camera footage on the engineering floor — physical access by third parties cannot be excluded. Her vehicle was demonstrably not in the office garage on the night of the offence.
translations.t0040: Bernasconi has a strong alibi supported by three independent card records and a physical receipt: she was demonstrably in Winterthur at 23:04 CEST (offence start: 23:10 CEST, St. Gallen). Driving time St. Gallen–Winterthur ~40–50 minutes; timely arrival at the scene of the offence would have been physically impossible. Further card records place her at 06:15 CEST and 07:32 CEST still on the route Winterthur–Flims, well after the end of the offence (05:58 CEST).
translations.t0041: Whether Bernasconi is among the 9 accounts that accessed Yannick's Confluence page (Real/Decoy mapping) is unresolved — no named breakdown appears in the file.
translations.t0042: Bernasconi demonstrably knew the pipeline's decompression behaviour (perpetrator knowledge K3) and had the 'delete snapshot and restart job' pattern from her own practice (S1). This knowledge point is not exculpated, but given the alibi for the time of the offence, it has no operative relevance.
translations.t0043: The friend in Winterthur with whom Bernasconi claims to have spent the night has given no statement in the file. The overnight stay itself is unsubstantiated, although the temporal context is consistent with the card records.
translations.t0044: Three independent, timestamped sources (card feed UTC, physical receipt with terminal time, service station receipt on the Flims route) establish Bernasconi's presence in Winterthur at 23:04 CEST — six minutes before the start of the offence in St. Gallen (~40–50 minutes' drive away). This is physically incompatible with perpetration at the scene. Additionally, there is no garage entry for her vehicle on the night of the offence, and June Okada's witness account describes the garage without Bernasconi's vehicle. The small deduction reflects the unconfirmed overnight stay at the friend's place and the open question regarding the Confluence page.
translations.t0045: Chiara Bernasconi cannot be placed at the scene of the offence in St. Gallen during the period of the offence (23:10–05:58 CEST) by means of three independent card records and a physical receipt: she was demonstrably in Winterthur at 23:04 CEST (scene of offence ~40–50 min away) and again in Winterthur at 06:15 CEST. Knowledge and access criteria are partially met, but given the temporal alibi they carry no operative relevance to perpetration.
translations.t0046: Whether Bernasconi is among the 9 accounts that accessed Yannick's Confluence page (Real/Decoy mapping) is unresolved.
translations.t0047: The claimed overnight stay at a friend's place in Winterthur is not confirmed by any witness statement (neither inculpatory nor exculpatory).
translations.t0048: The expense narrative 'drove to Flims after the candidate dinner' is imprecisely worded and was flagged by the finance system as deviating from card times (EX-L956: 'Narrative date differs from card times'), but was approved — no active contradiction.
translations.t0049: Bernasconi's knowledge of the decompression behaviour (K3) and the snapshot pattern (S1) is established; these knowledge points would be significantly incriminating in the absence of an alibi, but are irrelevant to the question of perpetration given the documented physical alibi.

translations.t0084: Ammann had the deepest knowledge of the Real/Decoy mapping, staging paths, and decompression behaviour — but this knowledge had been extended to at least 8 further individuals through Confluence (9 accounts), the board pack (Slide 11, Renata Vogel as assembler), and long-standing colleagues. translations.t0086: Ammann was physically in Lisbon for the entire offence window (23:10 CEST Friday to 05:58 CEST Saturday). The card payment at 18:05 CEST in Lisbon, the verified boarding passes, the hotel guest evidence, and the photographer's timestamps (NB-L72: 'Verified') make physical presence in St. Gallen during this window practically impossible. translations.t0088: The Slack message at 23:48 CEST ('collector window looks clean from here') shows active awareness of the logging window at the time of the offence. translations.t0089: It remains unresolved whether Ammann could have acted as coordinator or information source for another person — for example by passing on the Real/Decoy list. The file contains no positive evidence for this, but also no conclusive examination of the question.
translations.t0090: The alibi is established by multiple independent sources: card payment in Lisbon on the day of the offence (18:05 CEST), verified boarding passes, hotel receipt, calendar, and timestamped photographer raw files (all confirmed by the investigator in NB-L72). Physical presence in St. Gallen during the offence window (23:10–05:58 CEST) is practically incompatible with presence in Lisbon. No garage entry for ZH 610 882 in October. The remaining 9% uncertainty arises from: (1) no direct flight ticket timestamp for the return flight in the file (only NB-L72 confirmation), (2) no conclusive examination of a possible coordinator role, (3) significant financial motive remains.
translations.t0091: Iris Ammann was physically in Lisbon for the entire offence window (23:10–05:58 CEST), established by a card payment on the day of the offence, hotel receipt, calendar entries, boarding passes, and timestamped wedding photos — all confirmed as verified by the investigator. Her considerable expertise and financial motive are real, but not proof of perpetration; physical presence in St. Gallen on the night of the offence is practically ruled out by the documentary record.
